rows.say: What should I ask them about the grant before I sign?

The five questions that price the grant — ask them before you sign. Ask these before you sign — each one prices the grant or removes a surprise (your stated grant: 000 shares alongside $95,000 base, honestly unvalued until questions 1 and 4 are answered): 1) The strike price and the last 409A valuation — what the shares are valued at today, and when that valuation was set; 2) the vesting schedule and the cliff — four years with a one-year cliff is the common shape, but yours is what the letter says. 3) The exercise window if you leave — 90 days is the trap to look for; 4) your shares as a percentage of the fully diluted total — a count alone means nothing; 5) any liquidity path — secondaries, tender offers, or none until an exit.

rows.say: Walk me through the three financial statements
rows.delivered:
The three financial statements, walked through — statements, linkages, and the flow-through. Different thread, answered on its own terms: that is a finance technical, so it is served from the finance bank — your software engineering prep thread stays exactly where it was. The three are the income statement (revenue down to net income for a period), the balance sheet (assets = liabilities + shareholders' equity at a point in time), and the cash flow statement (the period's real cash movement across operating, investing, and financing).
They link at net income: the income statement's bottom line flows into retained earnings on the balance sheet, and it is the first line of the cash flow statement, which adjusts it for non-cash items and working-capital changes to reach actual cash. The follow-up the interviewer always asks is the flow-through: a $10 rise in depreciation at a 40% tax rate cuts net income by $6, the cash flow statement adds the $10 back and nets +$4 of cash after the tax shield, and the balance sheet still balances. Grounded in the finance drill bank's own answer keys — the same ground truth (fin-1) your practice answers are graded against, not a paraphrase invented for this reply.
